results.title: The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Tandoh, has called on the Government of China to treat illegal mining by its n
results.description:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Tandoh, has called on the Government of China to treat illegal mining by its nationals in Ghana as a bilateral enforcement priority, warning that the conduct of a "lawless minority" is undermining a friendship built over six decades.

Speaking at the China-Ghana Mining Cooperation Conference at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Mr Tandoh said the integrity of the partnership between the two countries is being tested not in boardrooms, but in Ghana's rivers, forest reserves and farmlands.

"Illegal small-scale mining has become an existential threat to our environment, our water bodies, and our national security. And in too many instances, Chinese nationals have been found at the centre of these illegal operations," he said.

results.title: The 2026 China (Guangxi)-ASEAN Mining Cooperation Conference kicked off on Friday in Nanning, capital of Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region in
results.description:
The 2026 China (Guangxi)-ASEAN Mining Cooperation Conference kicked off on Friday in Nanning, capital of Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region in South China. The event brought together more than 300 representatives and, for the first time, included Ghanaian mining officials in its training program. 

During the conference, Ghanaian delegation explored opportunities to learn from Guangxi's mining technologies and industrial experience. Through technology sharing, skills development and stronger partnerships, the two sides aim to support a more modern and responsible mining sector in Ghana.
#EnterprisingChina #MiningCooperation #ChinaAfrica #TechnologyTransfer #SustainableMining
